calls.head: Depth against star power
calls.body: On depth, the Islanders are one of the league’s best, but Ottawa is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Islanders.
calls.call: The Islanders spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Senators.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 64% chance, and they delivered.

NYI.head: We gave the Islanders only a 36% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: The Islanders’ power play hit a new low
surprises.body: The Islanders have had one of the league’s least effective power plays for years. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: 2.1 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 7.2 (about 6.6 against Ottawa) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

story.head: Pinto seals it in the shootout
paras: Artem Zub played his first game of the season, after missing the first seven, and picked up an assist. Ottawa had a goal taken off for offside midway through the first, though it didn’t end up costing them. Matias Maccelli got the scoring started for the Islanders with 12 seconds left in the first, but Ridly Greig made it 1-1 for Ottawa late in the second. Shane Pinto scored the only goal of the shootout for the Senators.

The Senators owned the chances, and still had to sweat it out in a shootout. Linus Ullmark made 20 saves for the Senators, and Semyon Varlamov stopped 18 of 19. The Sens moved to 6-2-0, and the Islanders fell to 3-3-1.

items.text: Matias Maccelli has a point in five straight games.
